about: Settings for the whole proxy. Listeners may override some of them.

keys.meaning: Seconds to receive the whole ClientHello; a slow trickle can't extend it.
Seconds to resolve and connect to the target.
Close after N seconds with no traffic either way. 0 = never.
After one side closes, the other side gets N seconds. 0 = unlimited.
Open connections at most; more are rejected.
Connections from one source (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64) still sending their ClientHello. 0 = unlimited.
Addresses or networks that may send a PROXY protocol header (v1 or v2), separated by ;. (Called proxy_protocol_from before v1.5.0.)
Bytes moved per step in each direction: the splice pipe size, or the size of each pooled buffer. Clamped to 4096..131072.
Free buffers kept for reuse.
Linux: relay passed-through connections with splice(2), without copying them through the proxy.

Remember a hash of every ClientHello passed through for 10 seconds (at most 1M, newest win) and refuse one that comes in again: it is this proxy's own connection come back (a name or ${host} target that points at this machine), which would otherwise loop until max_connections. Terminated connections are not covered.

Also listen on port 80 (every address the listeners use) and answer each plain HTTP request with a redirect to the same URL on https://: 301 for GET and HEAD, 308 for other methods. Every name is redirected; the HTTPS listeners' rules decide from there. The listener is named http-to-https-redirect (a reserved name); the console can stop and start it.
Pause N microseconds after a short read so data batches up. 0 = off.
Cached allowed name → target decisions. 0 = off.
Cached denied names, kept apart from the allowed ones. 0 = off.
Check the file every N seconds and apply changes (minimum 5). 0 = only on console saves.
Log a one-line summary every N seconds. 0 = never.
Where automatic certificates and the ACME account key are stored.
Where your own CAs live, one folder each (ca001, ca002, ...), with the certificates they issued: see cert = local-ca.
Renew this many days before expiry (or at a third of the lifetime left, if later).
Must be true for cert = auto: you accept the CA's terms of service.
Contact address for the ACME account.
ACME directory URL.
Extra root CA for the ACME server's own HTTPS (a private CA, Pebble).
cert = auto only asks the CA when the name resolves to one of these addresses, separated by ;.

keys.default: required with cert = auto and public_ip_address
keys.meaning: Public DNS servers for that check, IP or IP:port: three attempts, each the next server in turn, 3 s each; no answer means no certificate is requested. E.g. 1.1.1.1; 8.8.8.8; 2606:4700:4700::1111.
Legacy: accepted and ignored.
Legacy: accepted and ignored.

about: A port with its own rules; at least one is required. Overrides apply to this listener only.

keys.meaning: Up to 64 letters, digits, spaces and -_@#~()[]<>"'; unique ignoring case. What listener = in a rule refers to.
Listen address: 0.0.0.0 all IPv4, :: all IPv6 and IPv4, or addresses separated by ;.
Listen port. Two listeners can't share a port on the same or a wildcard address.
Overrides [global] for this listener.
A cap for this listener, on top of the global one.
Overrides [global] for this listener.
Overrides [global] for this listener.
Overrides [global] for this listener.
Shared by every connection on this listener, each direction, on top of each rule's limits. E.g. 1Gbit, 100MB/s, 64MiB/s.
For each connection on this listener, each direction.

about: A rule. The most specific pattern wins: literal names, then wildcards (more fixed characters first), then ANY. A name no rule matches is denied.

keys.meaning: The [[listener]] this rule belongs to.
A host name with * wildcards (a * never crosses a dot; as a whole label it is exactly one label), NONE for clients without SNI, or ANY for everything.
allow or deny. deny answers with a TLS access_denied alert.
Where to connect. ${1}, ${2}, ... are what each * matched; ${host} (or ${0}) is the whole name. Always in braces.
Target port.
Terminate TLS here: auto (ACME, TLS-ALPN-01); or local-ca / local-ca:ca002 (your own CA in ca_root, made on the CAs page, issuing one certificate per name on first use).

cert = auto: exact names to issue, separated by , or ;. cert = local-ca: names or globs (*.dev.example.com, several) that get a certificate; any other name is refused (default: every name the rule matches). With NONE or ANY it may list IP addresses: a client without a host name gets one certificate for all of them (and a NONE rule's names), otherwise one for the address it connected to; an IP address a client sends as SNI must be listed.
cert = auto: a script that decides per name not in cert_domains; exit 0 = issue.
The script's arguments, a TOML array of strings with ${1}, ${host} ... filled in.
Terminated rules: speak TLS to the target; false = plaintext.
Verify the target's certificate.
SNI sent to the target and checked in its certificate.
Send the target a PROXY protocol header with the client's address.
PROXY protocol version, 1 or 2.
Shared by every connection of this rule, each direction. E.g. 1Gbit, 100MB/s, 64MiB/s.
For each connection of this rule, each direction.

Serve HTTP here instead of connecting to a target (any key starting service_rule; needs cert, and no target_host, upstream_* or proxy). Options separated by ;: type=reverse_proxy; prefix=/api/; target=http://127.0.0.1:8080 (or https://; tls_verify=false to skip checking its certificate); strip_prefix=true; force_host=name. Or type=static_content; prefix=/assets/; base_dir=/opt/www/assets (prefix stands for base_dir: /assets/a.css is base_dir/a.css; no listings, no hidden files but .well-known). basic_auth=<[[basic_auth]] name> on either. The longest prefix wins; none = 404. The client's address goes upstream as X-Forwarded-For; what it sent is replaced.

about: Users and passwords that service rules can ask for (basic_auth=<name> in a service_rule). A password a browser sends is checked once and remembered for 5 minutes.

keys.meaning: What basic_auth= in a service_rule names. A second section with the same name replaces the first.

Any key starting user: username=<name>; password_hash=<hash> (argon2id, or pbkdf2-sha256; make one with tlsproxy --hash-password), or password_plain=<password> (no ; in it). A key given twice keeps its last value.

about: Where the two log streams go: activity (stdout) and problems (stderr).

keys.meaning: File for activity: accepted, route, connected, closed, stats, reloads.
File for problems.
Rotate a file once it reaches this size (K, M, G).
Rotated generations kept: file.1 (newest) .. file.N.
Generations above this number are gzip-compressed.

about: This web console, in console.toml (given with --console), not in this file: the console can't change it. It is read again on every reload.

keys.meaning: Addresses, separated by ;. With cert: the [[listener]] with exactly this bind and port serves the console (one of its own if none has).
Console port, e.g. 443 to share a listener.
The name the console is served under, as a rule of its listener that config.toml can't override.
auto or local-ca / local-ca:ca002: serve the console over TLS. Without it, plain HTTP on bind:port (keep it on loopback); a change of bind or port then needs a restart.
Plain text; replaced by password_hash when the proxy starts.
$argon2id$... (or pbkdf2-sha256$... from older versions); make one with tlsproxy --hash-password.
Plain HTTP only: mark the session cookie Secure, when another proxy publishes the console over HTTPS.
Plain HTTP only: names the console may be addressed by, besides IP addresses and localhost.
